Deutsch 한국어 日本語  ログイン 割引  Tradingkey 分析 株式 今週の予定：米8月PCEと9月非農業部門雇用者数が焦点、マイクロン決算に注目 TradingKey 著者 Alan Long Sep 27, 2026 6:00 AM AIポッドキャスト  すべてのコメントを見る （ 0 ）  米国市場は来週、8月PCE物価指数や9月雇用統計などの重要マクロ経済データを控え、FRBの今後の金融政策を評価する crucial な局面を迎える。インフレ率や雇用データが予想を上回れば追加利上げ観測が強まり、米国債利回りや米ドルを支える要因となる一方、減速すればハイテク株を下支えする可能性がある。また、マイクロン・テクノロジーやナイキの決算発表も予定されており、AIメモリ需要や消費動向の持続性が注目される。経済指標の結果次第で市場のボラティリティが高まるリスクに留意が必要である。 AI生成要約 TradingKey - 来週（米東部時間9月28日〜10月2日）、米国市場は9月下旬から10月上旬にかけて最もマクロ経済データが集中する重要局面を迎える。米国の8月PCE（個人消費支出）物価指数、9月非農業部門雇用者数報告、ADP雇用統計、JOLTS求人件数、ISM製造業景況指数が相次いで発表され、市場が米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）の今後の金利パスを評価するための最新の判断材料を提供する。 米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）は9月16日の会合で25ベーシスポイント（bp）の利上げを実施し、フェデラルファンド（FF）金利の誘導目標レンジを3.75%〜4.00%に引き上げた。利上げは3年ぶりとなる。最新の経済見通しによると、FOMC（連邦公開市場委員会）参加者による2026年末時点のFF金利予想の中央値は4.1%となっており、年内に追加利上げが行われるかどうかは今後のインフレおよび雇用データ次第であることを示唆している。 そのため、来週水曜日に発表されるコアPCEデータと金曜日の非農業部門雇用者数報告は、市場にとって最も重要な2つの指標となる。インフレ率がFRBの目標を上回り続け、労働市場が堅調を維持すれば、市場では年内の追加利上げ観測が再び高まる可能性がある。一方、PCEが減速し雇用増加ペースが大幅に鈍化すれば、米国債利回りと米ドルは圧迫される可能性がある一方、高バリュエーションのハイテク株は下支えを受ける可能性がある。 企業動向としては、メモリー半導体大手のマイクロン・テクノロジー（ MU ）が水曜日の取引終了後に2026年度第4四半期決算を発表するほか、スポーツウェア大手のナイキ（ NKE ）が木曜日の取引終了後に2027年度第1四半期決算を発表する予定だ。 主要イベントのプレビュー 米8月コアPCE発表：FRBの次回利上げ観測が試練に直面 水曜日（9月30日）、米商務省経済分析局（BEA）は8月の個人所得、個人消費支出、およびPCE（個人消費支出）価格指数データを、第2四半期GDP確定値とともに発表する予定である。PCEデータは東部時間午前8時30分に公表される。 7月の米PCE価格指数は総合で前年同月比3.7%上昇、コアPCEは同3.3%上昇し、ともにFRB（米連邦準備制度理事会）が掲げる2%の長期インフレ目標を大幅に上回った状態が続いている。前月比では、総合およびコアの双方で0.2%上昇した。 市場予想のコンセンサスでは、8月の総合PCEは前月比0.4%上昇、コアPCEは前月比0.3%上昇と見込まれている。過去データへの大幅な改定がなければ、総合PCEは前年同月比で約3.8%、コアPCEは約3.4%に上昇する見通しである。 FRBが直近で利上げを実施したばかりであることから、今回のPCE発表の重要性は高まっている。コアPCEが加速を続け、特にサービス価格への圧力が持続した場合、10月または年内の追加利上げの可能性が高まり、米国債利回りや米ドルを支える要因となる可能性がある。 なお、BEAは今回の発表に合わせて、GDP、個人所得、消費に関する過去データを含む国民経済計算の年次改定を同時に実施する点に留意が必要だ。そのため、市場は8月の単月データに注目するだけでなく、過去のインフレ率や支出データの重大な修正の有無にも注意を払う必要がある。 9月非農業部門雇用者数が注目の的に：労働市場は8月の回復軌道を維持できるか 金曜日（10月2日）、米労働省労働統計局は非農業部門雇用者数、失業率、労働参加率、平均時給などのデータを含む9月の雇用統計を発表する。公表日程によると、同統計は東部時間午前8時30分に発表される予定である。 8月の米非農業部門雇用者数は16万2000人増と市場予想を大幅に上回り、失業率は4.1%に据え置かれた。平均時給は前月比0.3%増、前年同月比3.1%増となった。一方、6月と7月の雇用データは合計で5万5000人上方修正され、それまでの労働市場の軟調さが当初の報告ほど深刻ではなかったことを示した。 したがって、9月のデータは、8月の雇用回復が一時的な現象に過ぎなかったのか、それとも労働市場の本格的な回復の始まりであったのかを市場が見極める上で重要な材料となる。 雇用者数の伸びが引き続き堅調で賃金の伸びも加速する場合、FRBによる追加金融引き締めの根拠が強化される。逆に、雇用者数の伸びが大幅に減速し、失業率が上昇した場合、追加利上げに対する市場の期待は後退する可能性がある。 マイクロン決算に注目：HBMおよびAIメモリ需要の持続性が改めて試される 水曜日（9月30日）の市場取引終了後、マイクロンは2026年会計年度第4四半期決算を発表し、東部時間午後4時30分から決算説明会（電話会議）を開催する。同社は決算発表日を公式に確認している。 前四半期において、マイクロンは売上高414億6000万ドル（前々四半期の238億6000万ドルから増加）、非GAAPベースのEPS（1株当たり利益）25.11ドル、営業キャッシュフロー253億9000万ドルを計上した。同社は以前、第4四半期の売上高を約500億ドル（±10億ドル）、非GAAP EPSを約31ドル（±1ドル）と見込んでいた。 市場は、HBM、DRAM、NANDの価格動向や、AIサーバー主導のメモリ需要に深く注目するだろう。マイクロンはすでにHBM4の量産出荷を開始しており、HBM4Eの研究開発を進めているため、経営陣による2027年のAIメモリ需要、生産能力増強、設備投資に関する見解は、単四半期の業績数字以上に重要となる可能性がある。 足元でAIチップサプライチェーンのボラティリティが高まる中、マイクロンの第4四半期決算および次四半期見通しが引き続き力強い成長を示せば、AIサーバーやメモリチップ需要に対するファンダメンタルズ面での新たな裏付けとなる。逆に、価格設定、受注、粗利益率の伸びが減速し始めた場合、市場は現在のメモリチップの上昇サイクル（アップサイクル）の継続期間を再評価する可能性がある。 今週の主要スケジュール 月曜日（9月28日） 主要イベント：9月ダラス連銀製造業景況指数 米国は9月ダラス連銀製造業景況調査を発表する予定であり、米国の製造業活動、新規受注、生産、および企業コストを観察するための最新の指標となる。 火曜日（9月29日） 主要イベント：8月JOLTS求人件数、9月コンファレンスボード消費者信頼感指数 米国は8月JOLTS求人件数、9月コンファレンスボード消費者信頼感指数、および7月ケース・シラー住宅価格指数を発表する。 このうち、JOLTSは企業の採用需要が安定を維持しているかどうかを検証する最初の指標となり、消費者信頼感指数は雇用や経済見通しに対する家計の最新の評価を反映する。 水曜日（9月30日） 主要イベント：8月コアPCE、マイクロン決算発表 米国は8月PCE（個人消費支出）物価指数、個人所得、個人支出、および第2四半期GDP確定値を発表する。 同日には9月ADP民間雇用統計も発表されるほか、8月財貿易および在庫の速報値も公表される。 米国市場取引終了後、マイクロンが2026年会計年度第4四半期決算を発表する。HBM、DRAM、NANDの価格推移や次四半期の業績見通し（ガイダンス）が、半導体セクターの最大の注目点となる。 木曜日（10月1日） 主要イベント：9月ISM製造業景況指数、ナイキ決算発表 米国は9月ISM製造業景況指数、8月建設支出、および週次新規失業保険申請件数を発表する。米国国勢調査局は、8月建設支出を10月1日に発表することを確認している。 ISM報告書内の新規受注、雇用、支払価格の各指数が主要な注目点となる。製造業の拡大を示す50を上回る水準が維持され、物価上昇圧力が根強く残る場合、米連邦準備理事会（FRB）が金融締め付け姿勢を維持するとの市場予想が強まる可能性がある。 米国市場取引終了後、ナイキが2027年会計年度第1四半期決算を発表する。投資家は売上高の回復、直営（Direct）事業、売上総利益率、および経営陣による通期需要見通しの改定に注目している。 金曜日（10月2日） 主要イベント：米国9月非農業部門雇用者数、9月失業率 米国は来週の市場において最後で最も重要なイベントの一つである9月非農業部門雇用者数報告を発表する。データは米国東部時間午前8時30分に発表される。 市場は雇用者数の伸び、失業率、平均時給に注目しており、これらを事前に発表されたJOLTSやADPのデータと組み合わせて米労働市場の実体を見極めることになる。 同日には米国8月製造業受注も発表され、設備投資や製造業需要に関する更なる判断材料となる。米国国勢調査局は同データの発表を10月2日に予定している。 このコンテンツはAIを使用して翻訳され、明確さを確認しました。情報提供のみを目的としています。 原文を読む AI生成要約 TradingKey - 米東部時間11月23〜29日の週、米株式市場は米第3四半期GDP改定値、10月の個人消費支出（PCE）物価指数、米連邦準備理事会（FRB）の最新の地区連銀経済報告（ベージュブック）に注目する。これらの経済指標は、米国の経済成長やインフレの動向、そして今後のFRBの金融政策の道筋を見極める上で重要な手掛かりとなる。 決算面では、ヒューレット・パッカード・エンタープライズ（ HPE ）、アジレント・テクノロジー（ A ）、HPインク（ HPQ ）、デル・テクノロジーズ（ DELL ）、オートデスク（ ADSK ）、メドトロニック（ WDT ）、ワークデイ（ WDAY ）、ベスト・バイ（ BBY ）、ディア・アンド・カンパニー（ DE ）などが発表を予定している。 米株式市場は今週木曜日、感謝祭のため終日休場となり、金曜日は米東部時間午後1時に取引を早期終了する。取引日程が短縮される中、ブラックフライデー商戦が幕を開け、市場では個人消費の動向や小売各社の年末商戦に対する見通しに注目が集まる。 主要イベントプレビュー 米10月PCEと第3四半期GDP：インフレと経済成長が試される局面に 米経済分析局（BEA）は水曜日（11月25日）に、10月の個人所得・支出報告書を第3四半期GDP改定値（第2次推計値）および企業利益データとともに発表する。前者には総合およびコアPCE価格指数が含まれており、市場はこれらを個人消費や個人所得の動向とあわせて精査することで、インフレ圧力や個人消費需要を見極める見通しだ。一方、GDP改定値の内容次第では、第3四半期の経済成長の強さに対する投資家の見方が変化する可能性がある。 デルとヒューレット・パッカード・エンタープライズの決算：AIインフラ支出に注目 ヒューレット・パッカード・エンタープライズは月曜日（11月23日）に2026年度第4四半期の決算説明会を開催する予定だ。一方、デル・テクノロジーズは火曜日（11月24日）に2027年度第3四半期決算を発表する。 投資家の関心は、AIサーバーの受注や出荷状況、利益率、将来の業績見通し（ガイダンス）に集まる見通しだ。両社の業績は、データセンターの拡張需要や企業の計算能力調達動向を見極める上で、市場に新たな手掛かりを提供するとみられる。 アンスロピック、IPO後初の通週取引へ AI「Claude」を開発するアンスロピック（ ANT ）は11月19日にNasdaqで取引を開始した。同社はIPOの公開価格を1株あたり83ドルに設定し、9億8000万株を公開した。来週はIPO後初の通週取引となり、株価が公開価格を上回って推移できるかや、この新規上場株の動向がAIセクター全体のリスク選好姿勢にどのような影響を与えるかが注目される。 アマゾン・レオ衛星の打ち上げ：地球低軌道ネットワークの展開を加速 アマゾン（ AMZN ）は月曜日（11月23日）、ミッションコード「LE-04」のもと、アリアン6ロケットで36基の地球低軌道衛星「Amazon records.title: バイナンスUSのデリバティブ事業申請、米CFTCの本審査へ（あたらしい経済）
records.excerpt: バイナンスUSのデリバティブ事業申請、米CFTCの本審査へ 11/20(金) 18:41 配信 米国で無期限先物の提供を計画 ※写真はイメージです（PIXTA） 米暗号資産（仮想通貨）取引所バイナンスUS（Binance.US）が、米国でのデリバティブ（金融派生商品）事業に向けた申請について、米商品先物取引委員会（CFTC）から本審査に必要な情報がそろったとの判断を受けたと11月19日（米国時間）に発表した。 申請の対象は、先物やオプションなどを上場する指定契約市場（DCM）と、取引の清算を担うデリバティブ清算機関（DCO）だ。DCMの指定とDCOの登録の可否は、今後の審査を経て決まる。 CFTCの公開記録では、BAMデリバティブズ（BAM Derivatives LLC）によるDCMの申請は、11月19日付で「申請中（Pending）」となっている。 申請に添付された取引所規則案には、ビットコイン（BTC）とイーサリアム（ETH）の無期限先物の取引条件が記載されている。これらの取引の清算はBAMクリアリング（BAM Clearing LLC）が担う予定だ。 バイナンスUSは、必要な承認を得た後に米国の顧客向けに無期限先物を提供する計画だ。同社のスティーブン・グレゴリー（Stephen Gregory）CEOは、規制下で無期限先物などの暗号資産デリバティブを取引したいとの要望が顧客から寄せられていたと説明した。 大津賀新也（幻冬舎 あたらしい経済） 【関連リンク】 バイナンスUS、米国事業拡大のため10億ドル評価で最大1億ドルの調達を模索か＝報道 トランプ一族がバイナンスUSへの出資を協議と報道、CZは関与否定 バックパック、米CFTCの取引所・清算機関承認を取得。無期限先物提供へ 米民主党上院議員9人、CFTCに予測市場の地域制限撤廃方針の撤回要求 米CFTC、予測市場大手カルシに法的措置を警告か、新商品の届け出めぐり調査

CFTCが「実質的に完備」と判断したのは、実質審査に必要な情報が申請に含まれているためであり、登録の承認そのものではない。バイナンスUSは現時点でデリバティブ商品を扱っておらず、CFTCが必要な登録を認めるまで提供しない方針を示している。 取引所として登録されれば先物やオプションなどのデリバティブ契約を上場でき、清算機関として登録されればそうした契約の清算を担える。両方がそろえば、完全に規制の枠内にあるデリバティブを米国の顧客に届けられる体制になる。 バイナンスUSのスティーブン・グレゴリー最高経営責任者（CEO）は、顧客が信頼するプラットフォーム上で無期限先物を含む規制下の暗号資産デリバティブにアクセスしたいとの声を寄せていたと説明した。DCM・DCO担当ゼネラルマネージャーのカテリーナ・ディコスタンゾ氏は、顧客保護と市場の健全性、リスク管理を中核に据えて取引所と清算の枠組みを設計したと述べている。 同社は今後もCFTC職員と協議しながら審査を進め、数カ月にわたって進捗を共有する計画だ。 バックパックは3免許を確保 米国では同種の動きが並行して進んでいる。暗号資産取引所を運営するバックパック（Backpack）は11月18日、グループ会社が全米先物協会（NFA）から先物取引業者（FCM）としての登録承認を受け、会員資格を取得したと発表した。NFAにはCFTCからFCMの登録・監督権限が委ねられている。 FCMは顧客の先物注文を受け付け、証拠金となる資金や資産を預かる仲介業者だ。口座開設などの顧客受け入れに加え、マネーロンダリング対策（AML）や米財務省外国資産管理局（OFAC）の制裁リストに基づく審査も担う。 バックパックは11月16日、米国でのデリバティブ取引所と清算機関の承認を取得したと公表していた。CFTCの資料によると、グループのTLDクリアリング（TLD Clearing, Inc.）が13日にDCOとして登録され、TLDマーケッツ（TLD Markets, Inc.）は16日にDCMの指定を受けている。 事業者 取得・認定済み 審査段階 米国での提供開始 バイナンスUS なし DCM・DCO申請が実質審査の要件を充足 未開始（登録承認後） バックパック DCM、DCO、FCMの3免許 なし 未開始（事前登録を受付中） 注：各社発表およびCFTC公表資料に基づく。バイナンスUSの認定は登録承認ではなく、実質審査に進める段階である。 バックパックはブロックチェーンを基盤とする取引システムを通じ、米国向けに暗号資産などの無期限先物をレバレッジ付きで提供する計画だ。特定の出来事の結果に応じて受取額が決まる「イベント契約」も扱い、いずれも24時間365日取引できるようにするという。法定通貨と暗号資産を担保に使えるようにし、複数ポジションで証拠金を共有するクロスマージンにも対応する方針を示している。米国の利用者は各地域の注文を集約する世界共通の注文板を通じて取引できるという。 米国での取引開始日は公表されておらず、現時点では取引開始の通知を受け取るための事前登録（ウェイトリスト）を受け付けている段階にとどまる。 規制下デリバティブ市場への影響 両社の動きは、米国で規制の枠外に置かれてきた暗号資産デリバティブ市場の構図を変える可能性がある。無期限先物は世界的には主要な取引手段だが、米国の顧客向けには規制上の道筋が限られてきた。DCMとDCO、FCMという免許がそろえば、取引所機能と清算機能、顧客資産の預託機能を一体で提供できるようになる。 バイナンスUSにとっては、CFTCとの関係修復が事業拡大の前提となる。今回の認定は審査の入り口にすぎず、登録までには追加の情報提供や協議が続く見通しだ。バックパックが先行して3免許を確保したことで、米国市場では規制対応の速度が競争力を左右する構図が鮮明になりつつある。 日本国内から海外の予測市場にアクセスし、金銭や暗号資産を賭ける行為は賭博罪に該当する可能性があるため、取り扱いには注意が必要だ。

records.excerpt: アメリカの中間選挙で敗北したトランプ大統領率いる共和党。アメリカの力が弱まることが懸念される中、日本経済への影響は円安・物価高に追い打ちをかける“逆風”となってしまうことが予測される。日本に表れる様々な変化や影響を経済ジャーナリスト、荻原博子さんが分析する。 社会・事件 2026/11/22 《米中間選挙でトランプ敗北》日本の「給料」と「物価」はどうなる？…荻原博子氏が警告する家計へのダブルパンチ トランプ大統領 政治 ビジネス 高市早苗 選挙 経済 マネー 海外 印刷 目次 Page 1 ー トランプ敗北により“給料”にも影響？ 日米首脳会談に臨むため、迎賓館に到着したトランプ米大統領（2025年10月28日東京・元赤坂の迎賓館、代表撮影） 【写真】「マナー研修は無いの?」物議となった高市首相の“乾杯”シーン 日米首脳会談に臨むため、迎賓館に到着したトランプ米大統領（2025年10月28日東京・元赤坂の迎賓館、代表撮影） トランプ大統領の日本訪問時(2025年)。選挙の結果を受け、高市首相は「トランプ大統領と日米関係を揺るぎないものにする」と表明したが今後はいかに 物議が上がった高市首相のマナー（首相官邸公式Xより） 物議が上がった高市首相のマナー（首相官邸公式Xより） 物議が上がった高市首相のマナー（首相官邸公式Xより） 11月3日、4年間のアメリカ大統領任期の折り返し地点で行われる中間選挙があった。結果は上院・下院ともに民主党が過半数突破。共和党は敗北に終わり、トランプ政権への不満が表面化し、一強だった政権に陰りを見せる結果となった。 トランプ敗北により“給料”にも影響？ これは決して海の向こう側の話にとどまらない。経済ジャーナリストの荻原博子さんはさまざまな視点から、日本に表れると考えられる変化を分析する。 「今後どのような政策が取られるか不確実なため、直接的な影響は未知数。 とはいえ、アメリカがこれまでより弱体化することは目に見えていますよね。それにともなって、日本にとって最大の貿易相手国である中国や、ロシアの影響力が増すことに。 これまで以上の強硬姿勢を見せてくる可能性もあります。対外危機をより意識すべき状況になるでしょう」 トランプ大統領の日本訪問時(2025年)。選挙の結果を受け、高市首相は「トランプ大統領と日米関係を揺るぎないものにする」と表明したが今後はいかに 影響は外交面だけにとどまらない。選挙前から日本では円安や輸入価格の高騰が続いている経済状況で、今回の選挙結果は、さらなる影響がみられるという。 「アメリカがくしゃみをすれば日本は風邪をひくといわれているくらいに、敏感に日本経済に反映されます。 AI関連株の暴落も予想されていて景気の先行きが見えず、企業が賃上げに慎重になっていくことはありえます。トランプ関税については、一時の勢いは削がれると思いますが、世界的にインフレで、しかも戦争という大きな不確定要素があるので、物価は上がりこそすれ下がる見込みはないでしょう。 円安と物価高によって海外から物が買えなくなる『買い負け』の状況もあるので、商社勤務の方も業績に影響が出るかもしれないですね」（荻原さん、以下同） 企業の業績が鈍れば、真っ先に影響を受けるのは私たちの「給料」だ。収入は増えないのに、物価が上がっていくダブルパンチに私たちはどう備えるべきか。 「 先の見えない状況に対して、まずは支出を減らす努力をすることが、最大のリスクヘッジになります。 高額な保険に加入している場合は、その内容を見直す。スマートフォンの契約を大手キャリアから格安スマホに乗り換えるなど、固定費を下げることを検討してください。 また、働く余裕があったら、家族総出でしっかり働いて収入源を確保する。パートの社会保険加入要件が10月から改正され、これまでの年収約106万円以上の賃金要件が撤廃されました。今後は、勤務先が一定の条件を満たしたうえで、週20時間以上働くと対象になりますので保険料の負担によって手取り収入が減る場合もあります。その分働く時間を増やす、ということも考えましょう」 週刊女性2026年12月1日・8日号 facebook いいね X ポスト LINE はてなブックマークに追加 政治の記事一覧を見る タレコミを投稿する 今日の運勢を無料で見る コピーしました

records.title: 米ＦＲＢ、物価安定道半ば＝複数回の追加利上げも―ウォーシュ議長就任半年
records.excerpt: 米ＦＲＢ、物価安定道半ば＝複数回の追加利上げも―ウォーシュ議長就任半年 11/20(金) 14:47 share シェア X Facebook LINE 閉じる 【ワシントン時事】ウォーシュ米連邦準備制度理事会（ＦＲＢ）議長の就任から２２日で半年を迎える。ウォーシュ氏は利下げを求めるトランプ大統領に指名されただけに金融緩和に前向きとみられていたが、物価安定の実現を重視。ＦＲＢは９月の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で約３年ぶりの利上げを決めた。ただ、物価高は根強く、インフレ退治は道半ばの状況で、ＦＲＢ高官からは複数回の追加利上げを求める意見が出ている。 ウォーシュ氏は金融大手幹部などを経て、２００６年に史上最年少の３５歳でＦＲＢ理事に就任。０８年のリーマン・ショック時にはバーナンキ議長（当時）の右腕として危機対応に奔走したが、国債購入を通じ市場に資金供給する「量的緩和」の常態化に反発し、１１年に理事を辞任した。 １５年ぶりに議長としてＦＲＢに復帰したウォーシュ氏は、米イラン紛争に伴うエネルギー高などによる物価高を警戒する一方、金利動向を示唆しない持論を貫く。市場では同氏が利上げに後ろ向きと捉えられ、インフレ抑制が後手に回るとの懸念が台頭。夏場には米長期国債の利回りが急上昇した。 市場の警告に危機感を覚えた同氏は８月、年次経済シンポジウム「ジャクソンホール会議」で、基調的なインフレが目標の２％に戻らなければ、「やるべき仕事がある」と明言。利上げに含みを持たせた。ＦＲＢは９月、金融引き締めにかじを切ったが、人工知能（ＡＩ）ブームに伴う投資活発化などが響き、インフレ圧力は強まるばかりだ。 経済が底堅さを保つ中、セントルイス連邦準備銀行のムサレム総裁は「来春までに複数回の利上げが必要になる可能性が高い」と予想。「より積極的な取り組みが必要だ」として、ウォラーＦＲＢ理事は１２月のＦＯＭＣで通常の倍に当たる０．５％の利上げを訴える。 一方、追加利上げは「慎重に決定すべきだ」（ジェファーソンＦＲＢ副議長）とみる向きもあり、金融政策の展望を巡る見解は割れる。ウォーシュ氏が合意形成を図り、インフレ高進を抑えられるか真価が問われる。 ［時事通信社］ 記事に関するキーワード 物価 イラン 国債 連邦公開市場委員会 提供元の記事 （外部サイトに移動します） 関連記事 数カ月内の利上げ適切＝次回会合で大幅引き締めも―米ＦＯＭＣ要旨 records.evidence: Google News RSSで「米ＦＲＢ、物価安定道半ば＝複数回の追加利上げも―ウォーシュ議長就任半年」を確認し、配信元ページhttps://topics.smt.docomo.ne.jp/article/jiji/business/jiji-2026112000727?utm_source=dnews&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=contentsmatch17を特定した。本文抽出: 米ＦＲＢ、物価安定道半ば＝複数回の追加利上げも―ウォーシュ議長就任半年 11/20(金) 14:47 share シェア X Facebook LINE 閉じる 【ワシントン時事】ウォーシュ米連邦準備制度理事会（ＦＲＢ）議長の就任から２２日で半年を迎える。ウォーシュ氏は利下げを求めるトランプ大統領に指名されただけに金融緩和に前向きとみられていたが、物価安定の実現を重視。ＦＲＢは９月の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で約３年ぶりの利上げを決めた。ただ、物価高は根強く、インフレ退治は道半ばの状況で、ＦＲＢ高官からは複数回の追加利上げを求める意見が出ている。 ウォーシュ氏は金融大手幹部などを経て、２００６年に史上最年少の３５歳でＦＲＢ理事に就任。０８年のリーマン・ショック時にはバーナンキ議長（当時）の右腕として危機対応に奔走したが、国債購入を通じ市場に資金供給する「量的緩和」の常態化に反発し、１１年に理事を辞任した。 １５年ぶりに議長としてＦＲＢに復帰したウォーシュ氏は、米イラン紛争に伴うエネルギー高などによる物価高を警戒する一方、金利動向を示唆しない持論を貫く。市場では同氏が利上げに後ろ向きと捉えられ、インフレ抑制が後手に回るとの懸念が台頭。夏場には米長期国債の利回りが急上昇した。 市場の警告に危機感を覚えた同氏は８月、年次経済シンポジウム「ジャクソンホール会議」で、基調的なインフレが目標の２％に戻らなければ、「やるべき仕事がある」と明言。利上げに含みを持たせた。ＦＲＢは９月、金融引き締めにかじを切ったが、人工知能（ＡＩ）ブームに伴う投資活発化などが響き、インフレ圧力は強まるばかりだ

records.title: 韓国株、AI関連株安から反発なるか 米物価と金利に注目
records.excerpt: 韓国株、AI関連株安から反発なるか 米物価と金利に注目 - ChosunBiz 日本語 金融 韓国株、AI関連株安から反発なるか 米物価と金利に注目 25日発表の米個人消費支出物価指数が予想を上回れば、追加利上げへの懸念が強まる可能性 입력 2026.11.22. 06:00 업데이트 2026.11.22. 18:52 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 今週（23~27日）は投資家の関心がマクロ経済関連のイベントや金利に集まる見通しだ。エヌビディアの決算発表やAnthropicの新規株式公開（IPO）など、人工知能（AI）のバリューチェーンに関連する大型イベントが続くなか、先週急落した韓国株式市場が反発できるかが注目される。 KOSPIが下落して取引を開始した20日、ソウル市中区のハナ銀行ディーリングルームの現況ボードにKOSPI指数が表示されている。 /News1 先週のKOSPI指数は4900ポイントを割り込んだ。5375.36ポイントで始まったKOSPI指数は20日に4869.96ポイントまで下落した。米国市場に上場したAnthropicが史上最大の新規株式公開（IPO）を記録するなど、世界の投資資金を吸収したことで、既存のAIバリューチェーン関連株は大きな打撃を受けた。 今週の韓国株式市場では、まず米国市場の影響に目が向くとみられる。先週最後の営業日だった20日（現地時間）、ニューヨーク株式市場の主要3指数はそろって下落して取引を終えた。 特にナスダック総合指数は5.28%下落し、エヌビディアの株価は14%急落して52週安値を更新した。華々しく市場デビューしたAnthropicの株価も上場2日目に8.50%下落して取引を終えた。人工知能（AI）への懸念が高まっているだけに、韓国の半導体株にも影響が及ぶとみられる。 こうしたなか、米国の物価指標の発表が控えている。韓国時間の25日に米国の10月の個人消費支出（PCE）物価指数が発表される。米国の10月のPCE物価指数とコア指数の予想は前年同月比でそれぞれ3.8%、3.2%と、前月（3.6%、3.1%）より高くなると見込まれている。 米連邦準備理事会（FRB）が最近、物価上昇リスクへの懸念を表明していることから、物価指標への関心は高い。FRB当局者はインフレ懸念に先手を打つため、政策金利を一度に50bp引き上げる「ビッグステップ」の可能性にも言及した。 大信證券のイ・ギョンミン研究員は「PCE物価が予想を上回れば、追加利上げへの懸念と国債金利の上昇圧力が強まり、AI関連の好材料があっても株式市場の反発力が限られる可能性が高い」としたうえで、「一方、物価上昇の鈍化が確認されれば、金融政策の重荷が和らぐとともに、リスク資産への選好が回復するだろう」と説明した。 26日には今年最後の韓国銀行金融通貨委員会が予定されている。現在の政策金利は年3.00%だが、0.25%ポイント引き上げられ、3.25%になる可能性が指摘されている。 米国市場は26日に感謝祭のため休場し、27日は取引を早めに終了する。米国の通常取引時間が短くなることで、世界の投資家の取引が低調になる可能性が指摘されている。NH投資証券のナ・ジョンファン研究員は「外国人投資家の取引減少で韓国株式市場の需給も薄くなり、少ない取引量でも株価の変動が大きくなる可能性がある点に注意が必要だ」と説明した。 米国の年末消費が増える「ブラックフライデー」が本格的に始まる。先週、韓中首脳が会談を通じてサービス分野の自由貿易協定（FTA）妥結を宣言したことで、中国関連の消費財株は大幅に上昇した。ブラックフライデーの時期に米国の消費が大きく増え、世界の株式市場の追い風となるかが注目される。 大信證券のムン・ナムジュン研究員は「来週は年末商戦という新たな変数が登場する」としたうえで、「今年の年末の小売売上高は前年比4.5%増と、2021年以降で最高水準を記録すると予想される。米国株式市場は例年の年末商戦に伴う季節的な上昇への期待を織り込んでいくと予想する」と説明した。 ※ 本記事はAIで翻訳されています。ご意見は こちらのフォーム から送信してください。 Park Ji-young 편집국 증권부 기자 Park Ji-young 편집국 증권부 기자 Park Ji-young 편집국 증권부 기자 あわせて読みたい記事 あわせて読みたい記事 あわせて読みたい記事

records.title: 米海軍次官候補、韓国と日本の造船所は生産能力において世界最高水準
records.excerpt: 米海軍次官候補、韓国と日本の造船所は生産能力において世界最高水準 ホーム 米国関連 欧州関連 ロシア関連 インド太平洋関連 日本関連 中国関連 中東アフリカ関連 menu ホーム 米国関連 米海軍次官候補、韓国と日本の造船所は生産能力において世界最高水準 米国関連 2026.11.20 米海軍次官候補、韓国と日本の造船所は生産能力において世界最高水準 海軍次官に指名されたウィリアム･トティ氏は「もう海外の造船所で軍艦を建造する方法は支持しない」「フリゲートを最速で手に入れる方法はこれに特化した世界最高水準の造船所を新たに設立することだ」「艦艇の品質面ではなく生産能力という観点から見て世界最高水準の造船所を有するのは韓国と日本だ」と述べた。 参考： Toti pushes new foreign-built shipyard in the US to focus on frigates, large surface combatants 参考： Navy Wants New U.S. Frigate Shipyard Paid for by Foreign Shipbuilder 新たな造船所を建設して運営する直接的な見返りは50隻～65隻という次期フリゲート艦需要から生じる莫大な利益 トランプ大統領は8月13日に署名した国家安全保障大統領覚書の中で「沿岸警備隊の中型砕氷船計画で初めて採用された成功事例＝フィンランドモデルに基づき、米造船産業基盤への直接投資をさらに推進することを指示する」「海外の造船会社が米造船所に大規模かつ持続的な投資を行い、米国人労働者を雇用して育成するなら、一時的に最大2隻の海外建造を許可し、3隻目以降の船舶は活性化された米造船所で建造される」と明記した。 出典：Babcock この大統領覚書はフィンランドモデルを対潜･水上戦や護衛任務が行える水上戦闘艦、Ro-Ro型貨物船、洋上補給用の貨物･給油タンカーの調達に拡大することを指示し、その条件として「最初の2隻以外は新規に建設した米国内の造船所、所有権もしくは過半数の株式を取得した既存の米造船所で建造すること」「最初の2隻以外を建造するため米国人を雇用して訓練すること」「最初の2隻を建造した親会社の造船技術やテクノロジーのライセンスを米造船所に与えること」「最初の2隻以外を米国で建造する場合は必要な全てを米国のサプライチェーンから調達すること」を挙げ、この条件を満たすならバーンズ･トレフソン修正条項が免除される。 この動きを簡単に説明すると「海軍艦艇の国外建造（上部構造の主要部品製造も含む）はバーンズ･トレフソン修正条項で禁止されている」「米行政管理予算局（OMB）は海軍艦艇を同盟国の造船所で建造したい」「議会と造船業界団体は雇用を守るため海軍艦艇の国内建造を守りたい」「ホワイトハウスは同盟国設計の艦艇を取得して国内建造させることで雇用と投資を生み出したい」となり、上院歳出委員会が16日に発表した国防歳出法案にも「歳出法に含まれる造船資金で戦闘艦を海外で建造すること、米国内で建造される艦艇向けの主要コンポーネントを海外調達することを禁じる条項」が盛り込まれた。 出典：U.S. Air Force photo courtesy of UFC これで上院軍事委員会の国防権限法案による権限、下院軍事委員会の国防権限法案による権限、上院歳出委員会の国防歳出法案による予算、下院歳出委員会の国防歳出法案による予算の4つでトランプ政権、行政管理予算局、国防総省が進める同盟国設計のフリゲート艦を海外建造することを事実上禁止した格好になるが、議会や造船業界は同盟国設計のフリゲート艦を拒否しているのではなく「どんな素晴らしいアイデアでも国内雇用という利害を無視すれば実現しない」という点で、つまり同盟国設計のフリゲート艦を採用するなら「1隻目から国内で建造しろ」という意味だ。 海軍次官に指名されたウィリアム･トティ氏も上院軍事委員会の指名承認公聴会で「もう海外の造船所で軍艦を建造する方法は支持しない。現在は駆逐艦がフリゲートの任務を肩代わりしている状況にある。海軍にフリゲートを配備する最速の方法は、そうした艦種に特化した世界最高水準の新たな造船所を設立することだ」「艦艇の品質面ではなく生産能力という観点から見て世界最高水準の造船所を有するのは韓国と日本だ。したがって彼らの技術と生産プロセスを米国に導入することは、われわれの労働力と産業基盤を強化することにほかならず、それこそがここでの唯一の目的である」と言及。 出典：U.S. Navy photo Lt. Sydney Sisler Breaking Defenseも「トティ氏は海外造船所での艦艇建造という流れとは一線を画す、フリゲート等の艦艇を建造するため外国企業の資本･技術による新たな造船所を米国内に建設する案を提唱した」「海外造船所の活用を支持するのは補助艦艇の建造に限る」「フリゲートやその他の水上戦闘艦を建造するにあたっては海外の造船会社に投資させ、それらの艦種に特化した新たな造船所を米国内に建設することが最速の道だと述べた」「大統領が進めるフィンランドモデルでは最初の2隻は海外造船所での建造が認められている」と報じ、おそらくトティ氏が提唱する方式なら議会や造船業界も喜んで受け入れるだろう。 USNI Newsは潜在的な同盟国設計のフリゲート艦調達候補として韓国の忠南級、日本の改もがみ型、トルコのイスタンブール級、英国のアローヘッド140、スペインのF-110輸出バージョン、イタリアのFREMM EVOを挙げ、多くの日本メディアは一般受けのいい「どのフリゲート艦の性能や技術が一番優れているのか」を争点にしがちだが、トランプ政権、行政管理予算局、国防総省が進めているのは米国内に同盟国のフリゲート艦設計と造船能力を持ち込むことで、より重要なのは世界最高水準の造船能力を米国に持ち込むことだ。 出典：HD현대중공업 トティ氏は議会の支持を得るためフィンランドモデル適用＝最初の2隻を海外造船所で建造するという部分を削除した方式を提唱し、同盟国設計のフリゲート艦建造についても触れていないため、この取り組みで何を達成したいのかがより明確になり、世界最高水準の造船能力を持ち込んで国内建造するなら国内雇用は守られるので同盟国設計のフリゲート艦か独自設計のフリゲート艦かは取り組みの本題ではない。 仮に同盟国の造船会社が米国内に造船能力を持ち込むため新たな造船所を建設し、そこで自社設計のフリゲート艦を建造したとしても「自国の造船所で建造するのと同じ価格で供給せよ」という意味ではなく、米国内に造船能力を持ち込むための技術移転に掛かる諸費用については価格に上乗せしてくるだろうし、新たな造船所を建設して運営する直接的な見返りは50隻～65隻という次期フリゲート艦需要（レジェンド級カッターベースの次期フリゲート艦22隻の推定調達コストは約360億ドル＝約5.7兆円、1隻あたりの平均調達コストは約16.3億ドル＝約2,590億円）から生じる莫大な利益だ。 出典：Hanwha だからこそ欧州の造船所（英国、スペイン、イタリア、ドイツ）はトランプ政権が進める取り組みが本格化した場合に備えて準備を始めており、韓国のハンファオーシャンは50億ドルを投資して1億ドルで買収したフィリー造船所を「世界クラスの自動化とスマート造船技術を備えたデジタル対応の高効率造船所への転換」を急いでいるのだろう。 繰り返すが、この取り組みにおいて韓国と日本が評価されているのは忠南級や改もがみ型の性能ではなく「世界最高水準の造船所がもつ造船能力」であり、素晴らしい同盟国設計のフリゲート艦が欲しいのではなく「最先端の効率的な造船技術とノウハウ」が欲しいのだ。 関連記事： 米海軍の次期フリゲート計画総数は最大65隻、Flight IIでVLS搭載を検討 関連記事： Sections Home News & Events Press Releases Press Release November 20, 2026 Federal Reserve announces College Fed Challenge winners For release at 4:15 p.m. EST Share The University of California, Los Angeles won the 23rd Annual National College Fed Challenge. The University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) won the 23rd annual national College Fed Challenge on Friday, a team competition that encourages undergraduate students to learn about the U.S. economy, monetary policymaking, and the role of the Federal Reserve System. Teams analyze economic and financial conditions and formulate a monetary policy recommendation, modeling the Federal Open Market Committee. The team, from Los Angeles, California, represented the San Francisco District and included Aarushi Maheshwari, Annika Chan, Atul Prasanth, Caitlyn Cox, Finn Karish, Eli Brooks (alternate), Kennedy Yang (alternate), Manasi Vartak (alternate), Ronojoy Borpujari (alternate), and Sahil Sudani (alternate). The team's advisers were Chris Surro and Ali Haider Ismail. "I am very happy to congratulate the students who competed in this year's College Fed Challenge, especially the winners and finalists," said Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh. "They took on the same big questions we policymakers face. I'm impressed by their talent, their rigor, and their eagerness to think hard about monetary policy and the economy." This year's College Fed Challenge included 141 schools from 34 states across the nation, the most in the competition's history. Teams submitted video presentations or participated in local competitions last month. Twenty-one semi-finalist teams then participated in question-and-answer sessions held earlier this month, and seven finalists were invited to the Federal Reserve Board for the national finals. The other national finalists were the University of Chicago in second place and the University of Maryland, College Park in third place. Teams with honorable mentions include Cleveland State University, Harvard College, Pennsylvania State University, and St. Lawrence University. Teams were evaluated on their economic analysis, responses to the judges' questions, teamwork, and presentations. For media inquiries, please email [email protected] or call 202-452-2955. Last Update: November 20, 2026

records.title: Canada joins NATO innovation fund, promises ‘business as usual’ with US
records.excerpt: Canada's Defence Minister David McGuinty at a summit of the so-called "Coalition of the Willing," a group of Ukraine's most significant allies and supporters, at the Chancellery in Berlin on November 19, 2026. Kenzo TRIBOUILLARD / AFP via Getty Images Stay Connected Insights & Reports How to scale agents across defense and national security agencies Presented By Google Public Sector Download Now Reclaim the mission: A federal leader’s guide to outcomes- based managed services Presented By KPMG Download Now Policy Canada joins NATO innovation fund, promises ‘business as usual’ with US But the investment is a pointed reaction to the Trump administration’s dwindling cooperation with its northern ally. Patrick Tucker | November 21, 2026 06:16 PM ET Americas Pentagon NATO Industry By Patrick Tucker Science & Technology Editor November 21, 2026 06:16 PM ET Americas Pentagon NATO Industry HALIFAX, Nova Scotia —Hours after news broke that the United States would limit defense cooperation with Canada, the Canadian government announced plans to pour 100 million Canadian dollars into a NATO defense-innovation fund. “As far as we're concerned, it's business as usual,” Defense Minister David McGuinty said when asked about the news. It was a calm reply about an extraordinary development between formerly close allies, but in one sense, it was quite true. As the Trump administration reduces its contributions to the alliance—and in some cases threatens military action against its members—they are increasing their efforts to build their own militaries and industry. The Canadian decision pushes total commitments to the NATO Innovation Fund past 1.1 billion euros. Joining the fund also makes Canadian defense startups eligible to draw upon it, giving them another source of capital and access to the fund’s network of venture capitalists. The NIF is a way to connect startups with investors and military users across the alliance to “help successful solutions reach scale,” Tarja Jaakkola, NATO’s assistant secretary general for defense industry, innovation, and armaments, said at a recent NATO conference in Izmir, Turkey. In June 2024, for instance, German ground robot maker ARX Robotics raised 9 million euros in a seed round. The NIF led the round and provided more than half the money. In April 2025, ARX raised 31 million euros in a Series A round led by HV Capital. In July, Austrian venture capital firm Speedinvest led an 11 million euro extension, bringing its Series A total to 42 million euros. But competition for the money is stiff. In April 2025, NIF partner Patrick Schneider-Sikorsky said the fund had seen “thousands” of deals and invested in about 10 companies. Canada’s pledge is a bet on collective action. The funds could have gone directly to Canadian firms, and there’s no guarantee that any of the money will come back home. There is “no pro rata in the NATO Innovation Fund. It is finding the best technologies that best address the capability needs of the alliance,” NIF President Ari Kristinn Jónsson said here on Saturday. The announcement came hours after a White House news conference at which President Donald Trump again accused Canada, the United States’ second-largest trading partner , of unfair trade practices. “For some reason they feel emboldened and we can’t let them feel that way anymore,” Trump said. Over the summer, the president imposed 50-percent tariffs on several types of Canadian products, claiming that Canada discriminates against American autos, alcohol and cheese. But, as PBS has reported , Trump’s argument “rests in large part on retaliatory actions taken by Canada after the U.S. president imposed tariffs on Canada under the pretext that it should do more to stop fentanyl smuggling.” Shortly afterward, the Washington Post reported that Pentagon leaders had issued a secret memo restricting military cooperation between the United States and Canada. Canadian officials said they had learned of the memo from news reports and had yet to see it. In Halifax for the 18th Halifax International Security Forum, Sen. Mike Rounds, R-S.D., said the memo was months old and limited only flag officers’ participation in social events. Rounds said it “does not impact any DoD personnel that are in Canada today. It does not impact NORAD. It does not impact NATO operations or [the Five Eyes intelligence sharing partnership]]. Does not impact general or flag officer meetings.” McGuinty pointed to more than 70 years of military cooperation between Canada and the United States. “We have Canadian vessels interdicting drug trafficking in the Caribbean, working alongside American vessels. So that cooperation remains ongoing,” he said, adding that, as far as he knew, cooperation through NORAD and intelligence-sharing agreements continued as before. “As far as we're concerned, it's business as usual. records.title: Anthropic's $93.5 Billion IPO Marks Record Debut, Then US Stocks Plunge; Nasdaq Drops 5.28% in a Single Day, Erasing Year-to-Date Gains
records.excerpt: AI startup Anthropic completed the largest IPO in history, raising $93.5 billion, with shares closing up 17% on its first day. But the day after listing, US stocks suffered a violent selloff. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.28% in a single session, wiping out all of 2026's gains; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index tumbled 10.73%, and Nvidia crashed 22.92% for its worst weekly performance since October 2008. Markets are worried about further Federal Reserve rate hikes in December, $125 billion in new share supply in a single week draining liquidity, and the sustainability of AI capital expenditures. Historically, mega-IPOs such as AT&T Wireless, Blackstone, Glencore, and Rivian were all followed by market tops, but institutions generally view this round as more of a valuation and financing reset than a collapse in AI earnings, with the market set to move toward intra-industry divergence.

records.title: Fed monetary policy credibility caught between a rock and a hard place
records.excerpt: Fed monetary policy credibility caught between a rock and a hard place - OMFIF Skip to content Fed monetary policy credibility caught between a rock and a hard place By Mark Sobel / 20 November 2026 Falling behind on inflation amid myriad intractable challenges The Federal Reserve is rightly one of America’s most respected and revered institutions. Its leadership and staff are outstanding, and the Fed helped foster decades of price stability throughout the Great Moderation. Longer-term inflation expectations are broadly anchored. Yet, the Great Moderation is yesterday’s story. Today’s monetary policy environment confronts difficult challenges. The track record in meeting those challenges, which are often well beyond the Fed’s control, is increasingly mixed. That redounds negatively on the Fed’s credibility and reputation. Inflation The Fed states that delivering price stability is its job. But the Fed’s inflation target has been missed for six years. While roughly steady inflation of around 3% still allows households and businesses to make reliable non-distortionary decisions, the target is 2% and the difference compounds over time. Further, Americans are increasingly inflation-sensitive, especially post-pandemic and given affordability concerns. Amid low persisting inflation, the Fed developed its Flexible Average Inflation Targeting framework. The pandemic then hit, along with fiscal largesse and supply shocks. The framework soon was blamed for encouraging the Fed to continue too long with post-pandemic accommodation and took on the aura of mistakenly fighting the last war. Inflation seems increasingly entrenched, given economic resilience, artificial intelligence demand, low unemployment, energy price hikes and tariffs. One can’t dismiss the possibility of a return to more moderate inflation near the target given a squeeze on real incomes and if, for example, oil prices fall and AI demand cools. Neither can one bank on that. Monetary policy is best able to deal with demand shocks. The economy has been hit primarily by a series of supply shocks, many of which are beyond the Fed’s control. The Fed has been somewhat cautious, questioning whether the shocks are transitory and can be looked through. But demand seems increasingly buoyant and second-round effects are apparent. Financial conditions are arguably accommodative and not likely to be restrictive. Many suggest the Fed is now behind the curve. Views vary between those who believe the Fed funds rate should move 50 basis points higher and those who are calling for 100bp. There is little doubt that Doctor Fed must administer stronger medicine. Communications Clear and transparent Fed communication with markets is essential, especially as monetary policy works through the transmission of financial conditions to the real economy. That is not now happening. Chair Kevin Warsh is opposed to explicit forward guidance and believes the Fed should speak less and listen far more to market feedback, rather than vice versa. Most agree that explicit forward guidance isn’t needed except at the zero lower bound. But they also believe that, even if the Fed has been too explicit, it still should remain an important voice in shaping market expectations and that the market will seek out Fed views regardless, looking to the dot plot and Fed speeches. Thus, they argue the Fed should clearly outline its reaction function. But Warsh’s press conferences are not seen as informative, meaning his views are not shaping market direction. While Warsh’s relative silence – or interrogation of reality – may signify he does not have to voice a hawkish stance that might upset super-dovish President Donald Trump, Fed communication is now seen as having deteriorated. This is a recipe for exacerbating uncertainty and volatility across the curve as global yields are on the ascent. The White House and Treasury Technical debates about the future of the Fed’s balance sheet, whether it strays into fiscal terrain and what it means for money market management rage on. But the bigger issue is what the obvious interconnections of fiscal and monetary policy signify for the Fed and its independence. Trump has continued to plea for slashing the Fed funds rate, saving the government from a skyrocketing interest bill now in excess of 3% of gross domestic product and greater than annual US defence spending. He continues to minimise America’s inflation problem. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent – unusually – has publicly weighed in on Fed monetary policy, calling for lower rates and suggesting that higher energy prices should be looked through. In an unsuccessful effort to curb higher long-term rates, Bessent has upped the pace of Treasury buybacks. Warsh has shown that he is a defender of the Fed’s monetary policy independence and disproven those who thought he could be Trump’s ’sock puppet’. But Warsh’s task forces are not dealing with the elephant in the room: America’s massive fiscal deficits . These deficits are helping sustain demand and inflation as well as pushing up longer-term yields. Beyond suggesting US fiscal policy is unsustainable, the Fed is gun-shy in speaking about the impact of fiscal policy for demand, inflation, the yield curve and monetary policy, perhaps so as not to perturb the president. But these topics are central to the Fed’s wheelhouse and America’s health. Are fiscal and financial dominance potential threats to America? The Fed-Treasury relationship seems far less smooth than in the past, further compounding uncertainty. The Fed is caught between a rock and a hard place. It is falling behind in coping with America’s current inflation challenges after missing its inflation target for six years. The challenges are generated largely by supply shocks – energy, wars, immigration crackdowns, AI, tariffs – over which the Fed has little control. But they now appear to be feeding demand. Communications have weakened, abetting volatility. A critical administration unwilling to tame its fiscal recklessness doesn’t help. Warsh’s Fed is increasingly behind the eight ball. Mark Sobel is Vice Chair and Chief Economist of OMFIF. Join OMFIF on 3 December for the next edition of the Chief economists briefing . Interested in this topic? records.label: npr.org
records.title: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year
records.excerpt: AI stocks have hefty market values and have a much bigger impact on the market's direction. They were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market. Business S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year November 20, 2026 5:11 PM ET By The Associated Press Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange in New York, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Seth Wenig/AP hide caption Seth Wenig/AP NEW YORK — A bruising sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks on Friday pulled the S&P 500 down 3.7%, dragging the index to its worst weekly loss in more than 18 months, and knocking the Nasdaq composite into the red for the year. The benchmark index is now in what professional investors call a "correction," having fallen more than 10% from its Oct. 6 all-time high. The last time the S&P 500 had a correction was March 2025, as the Trump administration's trade war rattled the market. Its weekly loss, marking its worst such decline since April 2025, as the trade war escalated, capped a seven-day losing streak, the longest such string of losses since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The Nasdaq composite, which is more greatly influenced by tech stocks, slumped 5.3%, pulling it into negative territory for the year. Its weekly loss was also just shy of its worst week since March 2020, when the pandemic ground the global economy to a halt. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, with less exposure to technology stocks, fell 1.9%. Chip stocks like Nvidia, Micron Technology, Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices bore the brunt of the selling, but other companies connected to the AI buildout tanked as well, including the optical products company Corning and the energy provider Bloom Energy. The AI lab Anthropic, coming off a successful IPO Thursday, tumbled 9.1%. The sell-off in technology stocks spread around the globe: Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi each fell more than 5% overnight. European indexes fell sharply as well. AI stocks have hefty market values and have a much bigger impact on the market's direction. They were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market. Technology Investors scramble for a piece of AI giant Anthropic in blockbuster IPO The AI trade has been losing steam partly over worries that AI stocks' big market values and heavy spending are unjustified. Fears of a bubble within the sector have also been exacerbated by the results of the recent midterm elections, with candidates advocating for a slowdown in data center construction winning at both the federal and state level. "The whole notion that AI can continue to spend unlimited amounts of money and support the stock market, I think the notion of that is ending as we speak, that's what's being priced right now," said Michael Antonelli, market strategist at Baird. "But I don't think that means that the overall bull market that started in October 2022 is over." Much of the AI rout was centered among chip stocks, which have been big beneficiaries of the build out of AI data centers. Advanced Micro Devices sank 13.3%, Micron Technology slid 13.9% and Broadcom fell 12.1%. The PHLX Semiconductor Index sank 10.7%. Corning slid 10.9% and Bloom Energy gave up 15.3%. Nvidia, considered by many to be the poster child for the AI boom, fell for the ninth day in the last 10, closing 13.8% lower. The chip company's stock was caught up in the market's anxiety about the strength of the AI build out, and more recently has been pressured by worries about its future following the sudden downfall of Jensen Huang, its former CEO and co-founder. Since the Huang scandal erupted earlier this month, the stock has dropped more than 25%. The big market debut for Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI tool, fizzled Friday with the rest of the tech sector. The stock fell 9.1% to $88.30, but remains above its IPO price of $83 per share. It was the biggest public stock offering ever, at one point surpassing $2 trillion in value. Anthropic's share price drop on Friday amounts to a roughly 23% decline from its brief peak of $115.10 a share set the day prior. That's an even bigger drop than the dive seen for Facebook (now Meta) in the early days after its May 2012 IPO. Market debuts for tech companies are often followed by a volatile period. SpaceX, which previously held the title for biggest IPO, rose nearly 50% in its first three days, but fell below its IPO price a month later. Outside of tech, though, most stocks were gaining ground. Cheerios maker General Mills rose 3.7% and homebuilder Lennar gained 1%. All told, the S&P 500 fell 265.44 points to 6,910.39. The Dow dropped 949.73 points to 48,147.33, and the Nasdaq lost 1,261.47 points to close at 22,617.73. While the stock market's mood has soured, the sentiment among American consumers appears to have brightened, a reversal of the dynamic seen earlier this year. The University of Michigan's latest index of consumer sentiment rose sharply compared to last month, coming in slightly ahead of economists' expectations. Consumers noted some relief from easing gas prices and improved expectations for business conditions following the midterm elections. Still, sentiment remains below where it was in February, before the start of the U.S. war with Iran. Treasury yields fell in the bond market. The yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 4.93% from 5.04% late Thursday. Brent crude oil, the international standard, rose 0.6% to settle at $92.57 per barrel, amid continued tension near the Strait of Hormuz as the U.S. war with Iran continues. Saudi Arabia said on Friday that Iran-backed Houthi rebels had fired more missiles and drones at the kingdom days after it launched a major air campaign across Houthi-controlled parts of Yemen. Iraq apparently reached a compromise with a powerful Iran-backed militia it accused of smuggling oil. NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. records.label: nbcnews.com
records.title: Markets plunge: Nasdaq erases 2026 gains, S&P and Dow enter corrections
records.excerpt: A bruising stock market sell-off continued despite a record-setting IPO by Anthropic, dashing hopes it would revive sentiment on the AI trade. The surging stock market of 2026 capsized Friday, wiping out gains for the year in the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite while the broad S&P 500 and the Dow entered correction territory, meaning they have declined 10% from recent peaks. The dramatic sell-off is raising fresh fears about the viability of the AI investment wave that had powered stocks and economic growth for the first half of the year. Friday’s declines were led by Anthropic, whose blockbuster IPO just 24 hours earlier now feels like a blip after the stock lost 9%, wiping out hundreds of billions in paper wealth and putting shares just a few dollars above the IPO price. Nvidia also dragged markets lower, tumbling about 14% following a Reuters report that regulators are looking into accounting irregularities at the chip giant. With Friday’s losses of 3.7%, the S&P 500’s seven-day losing streak is its worst since the Covid pandemic; the index is now up less than 1% on the year. The Nasdaq finished the day down 5.3%, and the Dow dropped 1.9%. The losses also sully one of the most visible bright points of President Donald Trump’s second term. Amid sticky inflation and frozen housing and jobs markets, U.S. equities were the one part of the economy that appeared resilient. The AI investment boom created seemingly insatiable demand for stocks among investors, minting multiple new trillion-dollar companies in the process. While Friday’s declines were stark, they were not sudden, capping instead a weekslong slide that began in early October as the combination of elevated oil prices, rising interest rates, mounting corporate debt loads, stubborn inflation, supply chain issues and a flagging consumer put increasing pressure on stock prices. The sell-off picked up steam earlier this month in the wake of Democrats’ midterm victories, which raised fears of a slowdown in the tech sector’s data center buildout. Losses accelerated again last week as the scandal erupted involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and advanced chips potentially being diverted to China. “The stock market is going through an AI repricing, reflecting an environment of slowing data center buildouts, reduced funding sources for AI-related projects and a slower trajectory of technology-related earnings growth,” wrote Richard Saperstein, chief investment officer at Treasury Partners, in a client note. “This has been exacerbated by the Nvidia crisis and the Democratic midterm win, which were a one-two punch for the AI story.” Alongside the stock sell-off, investors have increased purchases of U.S. Treasury bonds — a sign that investors are seeking more reliable returns amid signs of weakening growth from higher interest rates and a stalling economy in China. “The pressure is becoming increasingly widespread, and that’s been felt across other asset classes too,” Deutsche Bank managing director Jim Reid wrote in a note to clients Friday. For U.S. households relying on 401(k)s and pension funds for retirement, the downturn is especially unwelcome at a time when inflation continues to prove nettlesome. Kevin Gordon, head of macroeconomic strategy and research at Charles Schwab, told NBC News that markets are feeling particular pressure from an increasingly “hawkish” Federal Reserve that is signaling aggressive rate hikes in the face of unrelenting inflation. “They’re signaling that they want to be aggressive in raising rates,” Gordon said. Combined with a weeks-long downturn among AI and tech stocks, “we have dual forces hitting the market.” A prolonged downturn could begin to cut more deeply into economic growth, he said. “If you have enough of a protracted downturn, which we really haven’t had since 2007-2009 in terms of length and duration, that’s when you’d really start to worry,” he said.

records.excerpt: The United States has issued a security alert for its citizens in parts of Mexico's Sinaloa state after armed clashes, road blockades and vehicle fires The United States has issued a security alert for its citizens in parts of Mexico's Sinaloa state after armed clashes, road blockades and vehicle fires were reported following the arrest of suspected cartel figure Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores.In a notice issued on November 21, the US Consulate General in Hermosillo said it was monitoring reports of security operations and unrest in Ahome, Guamúchil, Guasave and Navolato.The consulate urged Americans in the affected areas to shelter in place, avoid non-essential travel and stay away from Mexican Federal Highway 15 between Los Mochis and Culiacan amid the risk of further violence.According to the alert, the clashes, security operations, road blockades and vehicle fires were reported overnight after Meza-Flores's arrest.US citizens were also advised to avoid locations where law enforcement operations were underway and follow instructions issued by local authorities.The consulate asked Americans to remain aware of their surroundings, avoid crowds and monitor local media for updates. It also urged them to keep family members and friends informed about their whereabouts and safety through phone calls, text messages and social media.Travel disruptions warnedThe US mission cautioned that the evolving security situation could disrupt flight schedules and bus services in the region. Americans travelling within or through the affected areas were advised to contact their airlines directly to check flight schedules.Local authorities had also urged residents to remain indoors, restrict movement and avoid Federal Highway 15 between Los Mochis and Culiacan, the alert said.The consulate advised anyone requiring urgent assistance to call 911 in Mexico or contact the nearest US embassy or consulate.It also reminded American citizens that Sinaloa is already classified under Level 4: Do Not Travel in the US State Department's travel advisory for Mexico, the department's highest warning level.The notice provided emergency contact details for Americans seeking assistance. US citizens in Mexico can contact the US Embassy and Consulates at (55) 2579 2000. Those calling from the United States can dial 011 52 55 2579 2000 or +1-301-985-8843.The State Department's Consular Affairs division can also be reached at +1-888-407-4747 or +1-202-501-4444.The consulate urged Americans in the affected areas to monitor official updates and comply with instructions from local authorities as security operations continue.You use AI every day. records.title: 米株急落はAIバブル崩壊か調整か S&P500のEPSは31.9%増
records.excerpt: 米株急落を巡り、The Kobeissi Letterは市場がファンダメンタルズ以上の悲観を織り込んでいると分析した。S&P500採用企業の第3四半期EPSは前年同期比31.9%増と、4年ぶりの高い伸び率を記録した。 米国株の急落を巡り、足元の下げはAIバブルの崩壊ではなく、健全な調整局面にとどまるとの見方が出ている。米投資ニュースレターのThe Kobeissi Letterは、市場が企業ファンダメンタルズ以上に悲観的なシナリオを織り込んでいると分析した。下落ペースは急だ。S&P500が10月6日に高値を付けて以降の45日間で、米株式市場の時価総額は約6兆ドル減少した。31営業日ベースの日次平均では、約2250億ドルが失われた計算になる。相場下落の発端として意識されたのは、巨大テック企業によるAI向け設備投資の急拡大だ。Amazon、Alphabet、Meta、Microsoftの4社の第3四半期設備投資額は、前期比369億ドル増の2019億ドルと過去最高を更新した。設備投資額は1年で2倍超に膨らみ、2024年第1四半期比では356%増となった。直近3年間の累計投資額は1兆6000億ドルに達しており、市場では各社のフリーキャッシュフローと2027〜2028年の収益性を懸念する声が強まった。政治要因も重しとなった。The Kobeissi Letterは、民主党が中間選挙で上下両院を確保したことで、市場が混乱した際にトランプ大統領が相場を下支えするとの「トランプ・プット」期待は事実上後退したとの見方を示した。金融政策面でも逆風が意識されている。米インフレ率は67カ月連続で米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）の目標である2%を上回っており、FRB議長は積極的な利上げを続けている。こうした環境は、AIインフラ整備に伴うコスト上昇圧力にもつながる。個別銘柄では、NVIDIAとAMDを巡る材料も投資家心理を冷やした。NVIDIAはジェンスン・ファンの退任後、株価が数週間で40%下落した。AMDについては11月19日、空売り投資家のリポートで中国向けチップ密輸を巡る疑義が提起された。Anthropicによる1000億ドル超の大型IPOも、市場の流動性を吸収した。機関投資家の需要は4000億ドル、個人投資家の注文は1000億ドルに達したという。投資家心理の悪化も鮮明だ。恐怖指数として知られるVIXは10月の安値から100%超上昇し、11月5日の上昇幅は2018年2月以来の大きさとなった。ヘッジファンドによるテクノロジー株からの純流出は、6週間累計で過去10年余りで最大となった。では、AIバブルは崩壊したのか。The Kobeissi Letterの答えは否定的だ。最大の根拠として挙げるのが企業業績である。S&P500採用企業の第3四半期の1株当たり利益（EPS）は前年同期比31.9%増と、この4年で最も高い伸びを記録した。実績が市場予想を上回ったのは13四半期連続で、同レターは「恐怖は大きいが、成長も大きい」とし、異例の相場環境だと指摘した。バリュエーションも低下している。テクノロジー分野の予想株価収益率（PER）は2020年3月以降で最低水準まで下がった。NVIDIAの予想PERは9倍で、S&P500構成銘柄の中でも割安圏にあるとの見方を示した。また、ジェンスン・ファン不在でも、2028年度の売上高見通しは約7500億ドルとされたが、市場は利益成長そのものを十分に織り込んでいないというのが同レターの見立てだ。規制懸念についても、悲観が行き過ぎているとの立場を示した。米国がAIを禁止すれば中国に主導権を渡すのに等しく、現実化の可能性は低いと指摘。規制強化や税負担増の可能性はあるものの、市場はそれ以上に極端なシナリオを想定していると分析した。さらに、原油価格が11月に約22%下落したことを踏まえ、来年半ばにかけてFRBの引き締め姿勢が和らぐ余地も広がっているとみている。もっとも、The Kobeissi Letterは底打ちを断定していない。ボラティリティが高く、流動性もタイトなため、追加下落の可能性はなお十分にあるとした。その上で、S&P500が足元からさらに10%下落しても、なお健全な調整の範囲内だと指摘。30%以上の暴落を見込む見方とは一線を画した。不確実性が後退すれば、2025年4月の局面と同様に、割安銘柄を狙う買いが優良テクノロジー株へ素早く戻る可能性があるとしている。

Newspaper illustration with a schedule of the cost of financial shares © Newspaper illustration with a schedule of the cost of financial shares ( Shutterstock.com ) by luchschenF Jeffrey Gundlach, chief executive of DoubleLine Capital, posted on X at 11:58 a.m. ET on Friday as stocks slipped: “YTD the NASDAQ has underperformed T-Bills .” At 12:41 p.m., he followed up: “YTD the DJIA and the S&P 500 have underperformed T-Bills.” He posted no figures, so we ran them ourselves. We used the iShares 0-3 Month Treasury Bond ETF ( NYSEARCA:SGOV ) and the SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF ( NYSEARCA:BIL ) as proxies for a T-bill holder, and as of the November 20 close, the numbers support him on all three indexes. On Friday, the S&P 500 fell 3.70% for its seventh straight loss and finished the week down 8.4%, and the NASDAQ Composite dropped 5.28% on the day. A sharp rebound could reverse this within days. If you’re determining how much to hold in cash, the result still shows what 2026 has paid for so far, and it shows the rate outlook going into the Fed’s December meeting. Stocks Trail Cash Even on Price Alone The S&P 500 closed Friday at 6,910.39, compared with 6,845.50 at the end of 2025. That works out to a 0.95% gain. The Dow closed at 48,147.33, compared with 48,063.29 at year-end, for a gain of just 0.17%. The NASDAQ Composite finished at 22,617.73, below its 23,241.99 starting point, and is down 2.69% for the year. Over the same period, SGOV returned about 3.3% including payouts, and BIL returned about 3.2%. Both the S&P 500 and the Dow are now in correction territory. Banking Dividends Leave the Result Unchanged Price returns leave out dividends, which help the stock side. The S&P 500 Total Return index rose from 15,220.45 to 15,522.21, a gain of 1.98%. Over that stretch, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( NYSEARCA:SPY ) paid quarterly distributions, most recently $1.888834 per share. Including dividends, the Invesco QQQ Trust ( NASDAQ:QQQ ) is down about 0.6%. The SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF ( NYSEARCA:DIA ) is up about 1.2%. Every one of those figures trails both bill funds, so Gundlach’s claim still holds once dividends are banked. Rising Short-Term Rates Made Cash Pay More The 13-week bill yielded about 3.55% at the end of 2025 and about 4.12% on Friday. Treasury’s coupon-equivalent yield for November 20 was 4.25%. The Fed raised its target range to 3.75% to 4.00% [ 1 ] in September. Markets treat a quarter-point increase at the December 8-9 meeting as close to certain. Bill funds hold securities that mature within weeks, so their payouts move up soon after each increase. SGOV paid $0.328581 per share in November, up from $0.300547 in October, while a 5.04% [ 2 ] 10-year yield raises the return stocks have to beat. Where SGOV and BIL Fit, and Where They Fall Short SGOV closed at $100.64. It yields 3.62%, charges 0.09%, and holds $118.17 billion, nearly all in Treasury bills listed in its SEC filing . BIL closed at $91.59, yields 3.67% and holds $50.11 billion. Both funds pay monthly, and their share prices just move because almost all of the return comes from those payouts. Treasury interest is generally exempt from state and local income tax. If the Fed starts cutting, payouts will fall quickly, and inflation reduces what the income can buy. Over long periods, stocks have historically beaten cash, so for investors near retirement, bills typically serve as a reserve for near-term spending that avoids selling stocks in a drawdown (that reserve is the whole point of what planners call sequence-of-returns risk, something we walked through in a free guide to the first five years of retirement ). Why SGOV’s Payouts Could Keep Rising Into December SGOV is built for the cash portion of a portfolio. Its payouts follow the policy rate, and with a December increase priced in, those payouts likely have more room to rise. BIL has a slightly higher stated yield. SGOV has a low 0.09% fee and a much larger asset base, which gives it a cost and scale edge over BIL for cash holdings. Two things would change this view: a sharp equity rebound that closes the year-to-date gap, or a Fed shift toward rate cuts that drives bill payouts lower. records.excerpt: Free Article Explore Premium Services The Nasdaq Just Triggered a Correction. 1 Move I'm Making Right Now -- and 1 I'm Avoiding Now is a good time to keep buying stocks if you’re diversified and focused on the long term. By Ben Gran – Nov 21, 2026 at 9:45AM EST Key Points Since Oct. 6, the Nasdaq-100 index is down almost 20%, and the S&P 500 has dropped by about 12%. The author recommends continuing to buy stocks with a well-diversified portfolio of U.S. and international companies. Selling stocks during a bear market is generally a move to avoid. 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF › The S&P 500 index ( ^GSPC -3.70% ) includes the 500 largest publicly traded companies in America. Its name is often interchangeable with "the stock market" because the 500 large-cap stocks in this index make up about 80% of the total U.S. stock market capitalization. So, when "the stock market" (as in the S&P 500) loses more than 10% of its value in a month, people get nervous. As of Nov. 20, since reaching its record high on Oct. 6, the S&P 500 is down about 11.6%. The biggest driver of this recent stock market swoon is the same reason stocks have been delivering such strong results since 2022: the artificial intelligence (AI) industry. Big-spending AI hyperscalers and innovative AI frontier labs have been buoyed by investor enthusiasm for futuristic technology that promises to boost productivity and economic growth. But to get to that bright future, these AI companies have been spending (and borrowing) hundreds of billions of dollars. Investors are starting to balk at the high price of AI. As a result of these AI fears, the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 index has fallen even further than the S&P 500. The tech sector benchmark is down about 20% since Oct. 6 -- heading into a bear market. It's understandable to feel nervous when the stock market is falling like this, but investors need to take heart, stay calm, and have confidence in the future. If you've been investing as long as I have (or longer), you've lived through worse than this. Here's one move I'm making with my investments right now and one I'm avoiding. Image source: Getty Images. One move I'm making with my investments: Buying stocks It's easy to say and harder to do, but it's true: When stock prices are plummeting, that's when I try to just keep buying more stocks. A 10% stock market correction or a 20% (or worse) bear market is ironically the best time to buy stocks. It means stocks are "on sale." So that's what I'm doing. I'm going to keep buying stocks in a diversified portfolio of low-cost index funds. My favorite U.S. index fund is the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF ( VTI -3.52% ) because it lets me own 3,511 U.S. stocks of all sizes and industries, not just the tech sector. VTI - Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF $340.02 -$12.39 (-3.52%) NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26 Key data points AUM $689.30B Dividend yield 1.16% Expense ratio 0.03% Top holdings AAPL 6.90% NVDA 6.43% MSFT 5.32% Additionally, times when the U.S. stock market is struggling can be good occasions to diversify with international stocks. I'm going to keep buying the Vanguard Total International Stock ETF ( VXUS -3.27% ) and its remarkably diversified portfolio of 8,874 stocks from dozens of other countries beyond the U.S. market. VXUS - Vanguard Total International Stock ETF $75.38 -$2.55 (-3.27%) NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26 Key data points AUM $160.60B Dividend yield 2.63% Expense ratio 0.05% Top holdings 2330.TW 4.00% 005930.KS 1.74% ASML.AS 1.40% Eviedence shows that corrections and bear markets are temporary. If you look at the long run of stock market history, the S&P 500 has always bounced back from even the biggest stock market crashes and economic crises. Because I'm diversified with a portfolio of thousands of stocks from the U.S. and around the world, I believe that there's never a "bad time" to buy stocks. The stock market might keep falling for a while, even after I buy my next shares -- that's OK. I don't know which individual companies or industries will be the winners or losers -- that's fine, too. By owning these index funds , I'm betting on the stock market itself to sort out the winners for me. Buying "all the stocks" this way lets me own a piece of the global economy’s long-term upside. One move I'm avoiding with my investments: Selling stocks It's usually a bad idea for investors to sell stocks during a bear market. It's a little like selling a car or a house that's underwater on the loan -- it puts you in a disadvantaged position and locks in your losses. (The only exception is if you have individual stock positions that you no longer believe in and want to sell at a loss for tax-loss harvesting purposes. That's a longer conversation to be had with a professional tax advisor.) With a diversified portfolio of index funds that I'm holding for the long term, I'm not looking to sell anything right now. That's because I don't need the money out of my investment portfolio right now; I need it 20 or 30 years in the future. I don't need to liquidate my investment portfolio for cash. I don't need my stocks to go up today or tomorrow or next year. I need them to deliver long-term returns for the next 20 years or more. records.label: fortune.com
records.title: BNP Paribas sees 'panic selling' as the AI selloff drags the S&P 500 into a correction and wipes out the Nasdaq’s 2026 gains
records.excerpt: The S&P 500 and Dow slid more than 10% below their records Friday as the AI selloff spread. Some on Wall Street called it panic. The S&P 500 fell into a correction Friday, and the Nasdaq Composite gave back everything it had gained in 2026. Recommended Video The S&P 500 closed more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record close, and the Dow also ended in correction territory. The S&P fell 3.59% to 6,918.45, its seventh straight losing session and its longest losing streak since February 2020. Investors were “panic selling” as they tried to judge whether enthusiasm for AI had peaked, Benedicte Lowe, an equity derivatives strategist at BNP Paribas , told CNBC . Anthropic led the AI slide, as Fortune reported Friday morning . The Claude maker raised $81.34 billion in an IPO that valued it at $1.414 trillion, and its shares fell about 9% Friday, their second day of trading, giving back much of Thursday’s 17% pop. Reuters cited worries about slower data-center expansion, higher borrowing costs and Jensen Huang’s departure as Nvidia CEO. Huang resigned on Nov. 12, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. The people with the most money in stocks already felt it. Those with the largest stockholdings reported a decline in personal finances in the University of Michigan’s November survey, which ran through Nov. 16, “consistent with continued AI-related agitation in stock markets,” survey director Joanne Hsu said . What the panic looked like Chipmakers took the worst of it. Micron , hotlink]Broadcom[/hotlink], Nvidia, and AMD were down between roughly 12% and 14%. The VIX, Wall Street’s fear gauge, topped 30 for the first time since March, CNBC reported. The selling wasn’t only in the U.S. Taiwan’s stock index fell 5.65% Friday, capping its steepest weekly drop since October 1997, according to LSEG data cited by CNBC . Japan’s Nikkei and South Korea’s Kospi each fell about 5%. Washington added to it. President Donald Trump threatened a “tremendous tax” on U.S. companies that build data centers abroad, CNBC reported . At midday, some analysts still saw a rotation. “Money is leaving tech, not the market,” independent tech analyst Luke Lango, editor of the Innovation Investor newsletter, wrote in a note at 12:59 p.m. He said the Dow and the equal-weight S&P were higher at the time. His advice: Avoid AI stocks “while they’re being combative teenagers.” He also pointed to credit: SpaceX had to raise the yield on its $32 billion debt sale to 8.3%, which he read as the “capital spigot” closing for weaker AI borrowers such as CoreWeave and Nebius. The calm-down chorus Most of the Street said the drop would pass. “Given the solid economic and fundamental backdrop, the move appears to be highly sentiment driven,” Chris Larkin, head of trading at E*Trade from Morgan Stanley , said in commentary sent to Fortune . He added that “only five of the past 15 corrections from all-time highs since 1983” turned into bear markets. Deutsche Bank’s Binky Chadha called the market “very oversold” and said growth and earnings remained strong, according to CNBC . JPMorgan Asset Management chief global strategist David Kelly told Seeking Alpha markets were overdue for a tech correction. Chuck Carlson, CEO of Horizon Investment Services, told Reuters the market may be in a correction within a bull market. E*Trade’s own research is less soothing. A March 2025 E*TRADE study of the 14 times since 1983 that the S&P 500 first closed 10% or more below a record found five became bear markets. But the index fell another 10% or more after closing in correction six of those 14 times, and in 1990 and 1998 it came within a point of bear territory. The median total drop from the record was 19.9%. The backdrop Larkin calls solid includes a rate hike on the way. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said Thursday the central bank will need to raise rates again because inflation is too high, Reuters reported. Futures put the odds of a December hike at about 95%, per CME FedWatch, with the 10-year Treasury yield near 5%. The Fed meets Dec. 9. Investors will find out then whether Friday was panic or just early. Generative AI was used for research assistance and/or transcription of this article. records.excerpt: US stocks closed sharply lower Thursday, with all five major indices down more than 2%. The S&P 500 was up as much as 1.3% early before reversing to close down 2.02%, its sixth straight loss. The Dow shed 1,101 points, and only one of its 30 stocks finished higher. Stock indices get beat up with the Dow, S&P, Nasdaq and Russell indices all falling more than 2% Stocks Greg Michalowski 19/11/2026 | 21:25 GMT , published 19/11/2026 at 09:25 PM Tags Stocks Summary The only victory was Anthropic. The rich get richer. US stocks closed sharply lower Thursday, with all five major indices down more than 2%. The S&P 500 was up as much as 1.3% early before reversing to close down 2.02%, its sixth straight loss. The Dow shed 1,101 points, and only one of its 30 stocks finished higher. Buyers had their shot early as demand for Anthropic lifted AI shares. That bid faded, and all seven Magnificent Seven stocks finished lower. Persistent inflation remains a headwind for valuations as investors weigh how long the Fed may need to keep policy tight. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.05% from 5.07% Wednesday, offering little relief for equities. investinglive.com US closing levels Dow Industrial Average −1,101.11 points (−2.19%) to 49,101.92 S&P 500 −147.83 points (−2.02%) to 7,175.80 Nasdaq Composite −550.69 points (−2.25%) to 23,879.20 Russell 2000 −59.18 points (−2.18%) to 2,655.13 Nasdaq 100 −599.21 points (−2.21%) to 26,517.05 Anthropic gives back much of its early gain Anthropic opened at $111.50, reached $115.10 and closed at $97.17. That was 17.07% above the $83 IPO price and 12.85% below its opening trade. The $81.34 billion offering was the largest on record. An offering that size can prompt investors to trim other holdings to make room, which may have added to the pressure on AI shares. No tears for the employees of Anthropic who on average are $40 million dollars richer today. Sellers controlled the breadth The S&P 500 had 446 decliners against just 37 advancers. On the Nasdaq, 2,578 stocks fell and 674 rose. Energy dropped 3.52%, health care lost 2.18% with all 45 names in the snapshot lower, and financials fell 1.11%. The Russell 2000’s 2.18% drop showed the pressure extended to small caps. Winners and losers Magnificent Seven — Amazon −3.87%, Alphabet −3.46%, Nvidia −3.30%, Meta −3.27%, Tesla −2.43%, Microsoft −1.97% and Apple −0.92%. AI and chip stocks — Nebius Group −9.39%, AMD −7.72% and CoreWeave −6.11%. Intel bucked the selling, gaining 1.92%. Other standouts — Ambarella +7.85%, Palo Alto Networks +6.42%, Western Digital +2.98% and CrowdStrike +2.71%. Other laggards — Zoom Communications −9.56%, Celsius −6.20%, Block −6.02%, DoorDash −5.80%, SharkNinja −5.75%, Nike −5.43% and Shopify −5.34%. Other winners...Anthropic Employees Anthropic’s IPO added roughly $7.7 million per employee in paper gains from the $83 offering price to the $97.17 first-day close. That lifted the estimated average value of employee equity awards from about $44 million to $52 million , before taxes. The estimate uses The Wall Street Journal’s tally of stock options and restricted stock across roughly 5,300 employees. wsj.com The $52 million is an average equity value. Actual cash proceeds are unknown, and the filing doesn’t disclose the median employee’s holdings. Awards vary widely, and vesting and lockups limit when employees can sell. Trading lesson. Use breadth to check the bounce. If the S&P or Nasdaq bounces next session, watch whether more stocks start participating and whether that improvement holds. A handful of large stocks can lift an index while most names are still under pressure. After a day when S&P 500 decliners outnumbered advancers by roughly 12 to 1, a sustained improvement in breadth would give buyers more evidence that they’re taking back some control. Anthropic Shares Slide After IPO as US Futures Fall and Global Technology Sell-Off Continues: Dow Jones, S&P, Nasdaq, Wall Street Fiona Craig Fri, 20 November 2026 at 4:44 am GMT-5 3 min read ANT ^DJI ^NDX ^GSPC ^IXIC Dow Jones stock ticker ©Adobe Stock Images US stock futures moved lower on Friday as investors continued to reduce their exposure to technology shares, with Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) falling in after-hours trading following its record-breaking stock market debut. At 08:06 GMT, Nasdaq 100 futures declined 195 points, or 0.7%, while S&P 500 futures lost 26 points, equivalent to 0.4%. Dow Jones futures slipped 31 points, or 0.1%. The declines followed substantial losses on Wall Street on Thursday, when the Nasdaq Composite, S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average all fell more than 2%. Anthropic's initial public offering had been expected to provide an indication of investor appetite for artificial intelligence companies. However, the strong demand for its shares failed to reverse concerns about elevated technology valuations and the scale of investment required to develop AI infrastructure. Joe Maher, Markets Economist at Capital Economics, said: "Anthropic's blockbuster IPO has failed to lift sentiment," adding that major stock market listings and increased equity issuance have historically sometimes coincided with market peaks. US Treasury yields declined as investors sought relatively safer assets, although expectations of further interest rate increases by the Federal Reserve continued to influence financial markets. Anthropic Retreats Following Record Market Debut Anthropic shares fell approximately 5% in extended trading after the developer of the Claude AI platform reduced its initial gains during Thursday's session. The stock opened at $111.50, approximately 34% above its IPO price of $83, before closing at $97.17, representing a gain of around 17%. The company finished its first trading day with a market valuation of approximately $1.7 trillion. Anthropic reportedly raised around $120 billion through its initial public offering and an associated private placement, surpassing the previous fundraising record established by SpaceX earlier in 2026. Despite strong demand for the listing, investors remained concerned about whether high valuations across the AI sector could be sustained amid rising financing requirements and uncertainty over future profitability. Asian Semiconductor Shares Lead Global Declines The technology sell-off extended across Asia, with regional equity markets heading towards their worst weekly performance since March 2020. A global stock market benchmark was also approaching its seventh consecutive daily decline, its longest losing streak in more than three years. South Korean semiconductor manufacturers were particularly affected. Samsung Electronics (USOTC:SSNHZ) fell 7%, while SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) declined 5.9%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE:TSM) dropped nearly 5%, reaching its lowest level in seven months. Chez Anbu, Head of Wealth Advisory at OCBC, said: "Anthropic's strong debut offered only temporary relief," as investors continued to reconsider elevated technology-sector valuations. Gold Heads for Sharp Weekly Loss as Dollar Strengthens Gold prices continued to decline on Friday, with the precious metal heading for a weekly loss of approximately 9%, its largest in eight months. The US dollar remained close to a 19-month high, making gold more expensive for buyers using other currencies. Expectations of additional Federal Reserve interest rate increases also weighed on bullion. Minutes from the central bank's October meeting showed that almost all policymakers believed further monetary tightening would probably be necessary to contain inflation. Oil prices, meanwhile, were heading for a third consecutive weekly decline as improving crude supply conditions outweighed concerns about renewed tensions between the United States and Iran. SpaceX Creditors Seek Protection Over Nvidia Chip Collateral Separately, lenders involved in a $43 billion debt financing package for SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) have reportedly requested safeguards concerning advanced Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips used as loan collateral. According to the Financial Times, creditors are concerned that placing the semiconductors in orbital datacentres could make them difficult to recover or sell if SpaceX defaults. The report said it was unclear whether the proposed restrictions had been incorporated into the final financing documents. Terms and Privacy Policy Your privacy choices

Which battered giant would I buy first? By Daniel Sparks – Nov 20, 2026 at 10:57PM EST Key Points The Nasdaq Composite ended around 13.5% below its October record on Nov. 19. Alphabet's revenue growth has picked up in every quarter of 2026, hitting 25% in the third quarter. Alphabet had around $265 billion in cash and marketable securities at the end of September. 10 stocks we like better than Alphabet › The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC -5.28% ) finished at 23,879 on Thursday, Nov. 19. The tech-heavy index now sits about 13.5% below its Oct. 6 record close of 27,600 -- a correction, though not a bear market. The standard line for a bear market is a 20% fall from the high. For the Nasdaq, that's a close near 22,080, or about another 7.5% drop from Thursday's level. I'm not predicting the index gets there. But a plan is easier to stick to when it's written down before a sell-off than during one, and mine is this: If the Nasdaq closes in bear-market territory, the first stock I'll buy is Alphabet ( GOOGL -2.70% ) ( GOOG -2.59% ) . Image source: Getty Images. Alphabet is already in a bear market of its own Shares of the Google parent closed at $272.66 on Thursday, their lowest close since October 2025. The stock's now about 32% below where it finished the day on May 13, at a record close of $402.62 -- more than double the Nasdaq's decline from its own high. A lot of that drop came in a single session. The stock fell about 13% on Oct. 29, the day after Alphabet posted third-quarter results showing slower Search growth, lower earnings per share, and a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow. In other words, the stock's arguably already taken the sort of hit a bear market brings, while the business underneath keeps growing. Profits are still climbing Showing how well the business has held up through the drop, Alphabet's revenue growth has accelerated all year. Sales grew 22% year over year in the first quarter, then 24% in the second, and third-quarter sales rose 25% to $127.6 billion. Operating income grew 30% year over year in all three quarters. And in the first nine months of 2026, operating income came to $121 billion, a 30% jump from $93 billion a year before. I focus on operating income because Alphabet's net income swings with the value of its stakes in other companies. Other income (mainly investment gains) added around $127 billion in the same nine months. That said, not every number is heading the right way. Last year's third quarter had a $3.5 billion European Commission fine, so without it, operating income rose more like 17% in the latest quarter. And as spending on artificial intelligence (AI) shows up in costs, the operating margin has shrunk. It was 31.8% in the third quarter, versus 34% in the April-to-June period and 36.1% in the first quarter. The money is already raised The second reason is the balance sheet. Alphabet expects to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, and management said that amount is expected to rise significantly in 2027. A bear market could make raising money for that sort of spending more expensive. But Alphabet has already raised a lot of it. In the first nine months of 2026, the company raised about $85 billion in new debt, about $43 billion by selling common stock, and another $19 billion by issuing preferred stock. Alphabet's cash and marketable securities totaled $265.1 billion at the end of September, more than twice its total at the end of 2025. Long-term debt was $125.1 billion. Yes, selling new shares dilutes current shareholders, and free cash flow was negative in both of the past two quarters. But with around $140 billion more in cash and marketable securities than in long-term debt, Alphabet arguably doesn't need a steady stock market to keep funding its build-out. Why wait for the line? Alphabet stock doesn't look expensive to me now. At $272.66, it costs around 18 times expected 2027 earnings , while Meta Platforms , another ad-driven tech giant, trades at about 17 times its expected 2027 earnings. For a business growing operating income by double digits, I think the price is fair. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary. $3.24T Day's range $264.22 - $283.15 52wk range $264.22 - $408.61 Volume 58.3M Avg volume 31.2M Gross margin 60.86% Dividend yield 0.32% I wouldn't argue with anyone buying some now. The reason to wait for the line is that a bear market would probably mark down many stocks at once. Deciding beforehand which one gets the first dollar stops me from chasing whatever happened to fall the most that week. Alphabet doesn't have to track the index, either. But if it just matched the Nasdaq's remaining 7.5% drop from Thursday's close, the stock would trade near $252, or about 17 times expected 2027 earnings. If the Nasdaq closes 20% below its record, Alphabet is likely where my plan begins. Sure, the index might never get there. records.excerpt: A correction is when an index falls at least 10% from its most recent peak, while a bear market represents a fall of at least 20%. Free Article Explore Premium Services The Nasdaq Just Had Its 6th Correction in 4 Years. History Says This Is the Likelihood of a Full-Blown Bear Market A correction is when an index falls at least 10% from its most recent peak, while a bear market represents a fall of at least 20%. By Bram Berkowitz – Nov 20, 2026 at 2:57PM EST Key Points Corrections are actually fairly common. Tech and artificial intelligence stocks that have been powering the market have come under pressure. 10 stocks we like better than NASDAQ Composite Index › Tech stocks are having a brutal November. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC -5.28% ) is now down nearly 17% from its Oct. 6 peak. A correction means an index closes at least 10% below its record, while a bear market means a decline of 20% or more. Several factors are weighing on the tech-heavy Nasdaq, including disappointing earnings from hyperscalers and a Blue Tsunami in the midterm elections that raised concerns about further regulations and restrictions on data centers . Add in the Jensen Huang scandal and a Federal Reserve leaning toward more interest rate hikes, and investors have plenty to worry about. This is the Nasdaq's sixth correction in four years, which have overall been quite prosperous for investors. History suggests these are the odds that the correction will turn into a full-blown bear market. Image source: Getty Images. Five Earlier Corrections, Five Different Triggers As I mentioned, while the stock market has had a terrific four years, it has been volatile and also had its fair share of ups and downs, including five corrections prior to the current one. October 2023: The Nasdaq closed 10% below its July 19 high on Oct. 25, as the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield pushed past 5%. The Fed signaled rates would remain elevated, and big tech earnings disappointed. This correction ultimately reversed course in November, as signs of inflation cooling and the Fed signaling it was done with its intense rate-hiking campaign. August 2024: A weak jobs report, soft guidance from Amazon and Intel , and the unwinding of the Japanese yen carry trade pushed the Nasdaq 10% below its July 10 record in early August. Later that month, former Fed Chair Jerome Powell's signaled that rate cuts could be coming, which steadied markets. March/April 2025: The composite entered correction in late March, then slid into a bear market in April, falling roughly 24% from its December 2024 record. President Donald Trump shocked the market by imposing high tariffs against most of the country's major trading partners. However, a major tariff pause on April 9 sparked a furious rally. March 2026: The U.S.-Iran war, surging oil prices, and doubts about AI spending left the Nasdaq nearly 11% below its record in late October 2025. An eventual ceasefire helped the Nasdaq get back to record highs just a month later. July 2026: A chip sell-off tied to AI profitability worries and rising yields dragged the composite roughly 10% below its June 1 peak on July 29. Strong second-quarter earnings and easing yields powered a rebound, and the index closed at a record in late September. Index NASDAQ Composite Index Today's Change ( -5.28 %) -1261.47 Index Level 22,617.73 Key Data Points Day's Range 22,513.01 - 23,837.76 52wk Range 20,794.64 - 27,599.89 As you can see, corrections are more common than one might suspect. In fact, a 2024 Reuters study of LSEG data found that the Nasdaq has experienced 24 corrections over the past 44 years. According to Dow Jones Market Data, the Nasdaq has extended a correction into a bear market about 37% of the time since 1971. The Odds Favor a Rebound, but Brace for Bumps The good news is that the majority of corrections tend to revert back higher. The bad news is that there is still a decent chance that a correction could morph into a full-blown bear market , and the Nasdaq is not far from one as of this writing. This is the reality for Nasdaq investors. Investing more heavily in tech can yield fantastic gains, but typically entails greater turbulence. History also tells us the Nasdaq has generated fantastic gains. Since the turn of the century, the Nasdaq has generated a total return of 467%, besting the broader benchmark S&P 500's total return of nearly 379%. This includes the Dot-Com Bubble, in which the Nasdaq lost roughly 77% of its value between 2000 and 2002. So, long-term investors can stay invested in the Nasdaq, but it really depends on your risk tolerance. If you can't handle big swings multiple times a year, then the Nasdaq might not be the right index for you.
